text: In molecular evolution, a dN/dS ratio (omega) greater than 1 for a protein-coding gene indicates which process?
choices: Genetic drift dominating entirely over selection
explanation: omega > 1 means nonsynonymous substitutions accumulate faster than synonymous ones, the signature of positive/diversifying selection favoring amino-acid-changing mutations. omega < 1 indicates purifying selection removing deleterious changes, and omega = 1 is the expectation under strictly neutral evolution; the dN/dS statistic is interpreted as a selection signature relative to that neutral baseline, not as a direct measure of drift.
